subject: Request: EU log hold & backup purge exception — HealthSync
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@healthsync.io>

Cc: Mark Chen <m.chen@healthsync.io>, legal@healthsync.io
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Request: temporary hold on EU logs + backup purge clarification

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As HealthSync ramps up testing in the EU region, our security and compliance team asked us to confirm a few specifics about Redwood's retention and backup purge timelines for EU customer data and associated request logs.

Specifically:
- Can Redwood place a temporary hold on deletion of request logs related to our account for the next 90 days (we anticipate a regulatory review)?
- What is the exact backup purge cadence for EU snapshots and whether we can carve out a single customer for a longer retention window?
- Any cross-border transfer steps we should expect if logs are accessed for support/escalation?

I've attached a short request PDF with the compliance team's rationale. We are hopeful this is a routine exception but want it documented for our DPA. Please let me know what information you need.

Cheers,
Emma Lewis
Head of Compliance Programs
HealthSync
Attachment: healthsync_log-retention_request.pdf
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on EU logs + backup purge clarification

Emma — thanks for the clear note and attached request. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Priyom (Platform) to scope what we can do operationally and contractually.

High level: we support per-customer retention exceptions in principle, but there are two buckets to resolve: 1) DPA/addendum language and 2) operational implementation (how we materialize a hold in backups and logs).

Kimberly — can you advise on the DPA amendment path (one-off addendum vs. schedule in our standard DPA)? Priyom — operationally, what's required to stop the EU backup purge for a single account and to flag associated request logs so they aren't swept by our retention job?

Emma — we'll aim to get a proposal back within 48 business hours.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-05T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on EU logs + backup purge clarification

Emma / Vivek — quick legal note.

We can accommodate a ninety-day retention exception for logs related to an active regulatory review, but we need:
- A scoped addendum to the DPA that describes the dataset (log types, time windows) and the exact retention period.
- A statement from HealthSync asserting the legal/regulatory basis for the request (to be kept on file).
- Approval from our privacy officer for cross-border access if Redwood personnel outside the EU need to assist; otherwise, we must route any access requests through EU-based support or via a documented process.

Proposed path: I will draft an addendum that:
1) Adds a short clause: "Customer-specific retention exceptions: Redwood may, upon documented request and subject to administrative review, apply a defined retention hold to the Customer's request logs and backups for a specified period."
2) Attach the HealthSync request PDF as Exhibit A.
3) Add an operational note requiring engineering confirmation that the hold is enforced.

I'll circulate a redline by tomorrow. If HealthSync prefers DocuSign execution, include the signer details.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data
Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@healthsync.io>
Date: 2026-10-06T14:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on EU logs + backup purge clarification

Emma — operational notes from Platform:

1) Backup snapshots (EU region) — we run a rolling 60-day snapshot retention by default with a scheduled purge job. To implement a 90-day hold for HealthSync we can:
   - Tag HealthSync snapshots with a retention_exempt flag and skip them in the purge window; requires a short maintenance window to re-tag recent snapshots (~1 hour).
2) Request logs — there are two stores: short-term request traces (14 days) and long-term immutable logs stored in cold storage (60 days). We can stop the automatic deletion of HealthSync traces by applying the same retention_exempt flag.
3) Access controls — any engineering or support access will continue to be logged and can be restricted to EU-based operators if Legal requires.

Work estimate: 4 engineer-hours to add tagging to backup pipeline + 2 hours to add administrative UI toggle + 1-hour test run. We can stand this up within 3 business days after sign-off.

Caveats: Extended hold increases storage billing; we'll provide an estimate once the scope (how many snapshots/log volume) is known.

If that timetable works, Kim please confirm language and we can prepare the operational ticket.

- Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
